$comment: Every figure this repository's documents state, and the derivation that re-computes it from
source. Read by claims.py, which is byte-identical across the three asset repositories while
this file is not — same arrangement as dialects.json and providers.json, for the same reason:
the engine is estate-wide and the content is this repository's.
A claim is `find`, a regular expression with EXACTLY ONE capture group, plus `derive`. The
expression must match exactly once in `document`. Zero matches fails — that is the failure
mode this kind of guard rots into, and a pattern that has stopped matching cannot be told
from a claim someone deleted. More than one match fails too: it means the figure is stated in
two places and only one of them is being checked.
THE TWO DEFECTS THIS FILE WAS WRITTEN AFTER. The section on the positive dialect said idea
drift rose from 2 of 15, when the three repositories' own scored artefacts sum to 1 — and it
said so in both game repositories because the paragraph had been copied between them. The
same copy carried '74 of them here' into aetherholm, where the figure is 92. A sentence
copied between repositories carries its numbers with it, and nothing was re-deriving them.
The pilot figures are sums over all three repositories' $pilot blocks, so a claim here is
checked against emberkin's, aetherholm's and micro-brand's scoring together. That is
deliberate: the row that was wrong was wrong in the SUM, not in any one repository's tally.
FOUR CLAIMS WERE DELETED WITH THE THING THEY POINTED AT, AND THAT IS RECORDED HERE RATHER
THAN LEFT AS A GAP. materialise.py used to state the Qwen challenger's completeness — 97 of
micro-brand's 98 entries, 134 of Emberkin's 137 — and four claims re-derived those figures
from candidates/qwen-image-2512/MANIFEST.json. The owner withdrew that model and the candidate
trees were deleted, so the derivations became permanently Unverifiable, which claims.py
correctly refuses to treat as a pass. Deleting the claims is the honest move ONLY because the
figures were transcribed into materialise.py's prose first and labelled there as no longer
re-derivable. A number that survives its source and keeps its confident tone is the defect
this file exists to prevent; a number that survives its source and says so is a record.
AND ONE MORE WENT WITH THE PILOT SET. `candidate.ungenerated(qwen-image-2512-positive)` pinned
COMPARISON.md's count of assets the pilot never generated — the figure that was 74 in emberkin
and 92 in aetherholm, and which had been copied between the two files with its number intact.
That is exactly the defect this file was written after, and the guard did its job for as long
as the manifest it read existed. The manifest was deleted with the challenger, so the
derivation is permanently Unverifiable; the sentence has been rewritten as a record of what
the last run reported rather than a live count, and the claim is removed rather than left to
report UNVERIFIED for ever. claims.py treats 'could not be checked' as NOT A PASS, and a
permanent not-a-pass is a broken build that teaches people to ignore the exit code.
